submission.justification: Sensor-T2 has the best resolution (6 um at 150 um in the 2025 sim) but is excluded: after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its efficiency is 82%, against the 97% requirement. Of the two sensors that pass, Sensor-T3 resolves better than Sensor-T1 (about 9 um against about 14.6 um). I scanned T3 thickness from 50 to 300 um. Resolution is flat at about 8.5-9.3 um between 100 and 180 um, and gets worse above 200 um and below 100 um. The 170 um point gave the lowest value (8.47 um), but the run-to-run scatter looks like about 0.3 um, so the minimum is not sharply defined. I did not simulate T2 or irradiated resolution. I did not scan T1 beyond 100 um, because it is about 5 um worse than T3 at both thicknesses I tried.

requirements.evidence: T3 at 170 um simulated at 8.47 um. This is the best of the radiation-qualified options, since T1 gives 14.6 um at 100 um. The T3 plateau is about 9 um over 130-180 um.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2)
requirements.evidence: T3 efficiency is 98.5% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. T2 fails at 82%. T1 passes at 99.2%.

requirements.requirement: One of the three listed technologies
